researcher_notes: Scope: EU instruments that shape green claims or hit Vietnamese exporters, plus national ECGT transposition in DE/IT/FR and four EU-member-state cases with published claim wording. Method: WebSearch + WebFetch on 2026-10-13. EUR-Lex HTML and PDF pages returned empty through the fetch tool, so article-level wording was confirmed through other official pages (Commission Q&A on Directive 2024/825 extracted locally from the PDF; DG TAXUD CBAM pages; DG ENV EUDR, ESPR and PPWR pages; DG FISMA CSRD and Taxonomy pages; Commission CSDDD page; EP Legislative Train; ESMA; recht.bund.de; Tribunal judiciaire de Paris; BGH; AGCM). EUR-Lex ELI links are given as official_url by the standard ELI pattern but were not opened. Cross-check against docs/08-knowledge (05/10/2026 note A.5): no contradiction found. Additions and corrections: (1) the revised ESRS delegated act adopted 03/07/2026 was still in the Parliament/Council scrutiny period in the newest sources; its Official Journal publication is not confirmed, so do not cite it as in force. (2) EUDR: the Commission's own country list shows Viet Nam as 'low risk'. Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/2102 adds soluble coffee (CN 2101 11 00) to EUDR scope from 30/12/2027, which matters for Vietnamese instant-coffee exporters, and removes leather. (3) ECGT is transposed in Germany (3. UWGÄndG, BGBl. 2026 I Nr. 43, in force 27/09/2026) and Italy (D.Lgs. 30/2026). France's vehicle (the DDADUE bill) was still at the Assemblée nationale in the newest source. (4) The Commission Q&A (September 2026) says sustainability labels set up by NON-EU public authorities are banned on the EU consumer market unless they rest on a certification scheme. This bears on Vietnamese state eco-labels shown on goods sold in the EU. (5) The CBAM downstream extension has its first political trilogue on 20/10/2026, one week after as_of. Re-check before the 25/10 semifinal. (6) The SFDR 2.0 plenary vote was expected in October 2026 but is not confirmed. Rule-engine guidance: per Commission Q&A Q1, EU consumer law (ECGT/UCPD) does not bind investor-facing annual or sustainability reports. Use the ECGT Annex I categories (generic claim, whole-vs-part claim, offset-based product neutrality, future-performance claim without a verified plan, self-made label) as a LABEL CONVENTION and international benchmark for Vietnamese reports. Do not use them as a legal finding. CBAM, EUDR and the EuGB register give quantitative or registry evidence that can confirm or contradict specific claims.
gaps: EUR-Lex texts could not be read through the tool; article numbers for Directive (EU) 2026/470, Regulation (EU) 2025/2083, Regulation (EU) 2025/2650 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/73 were not checked against the Official Journal text.

Revised ESRS and voluntary-standard delegated acts (adopted 3/7/2026): Official Journal publication and whether the scrutiny period was extended are not confirmed; Commission C-numbers not found.

key_provisions.ref: UCPD Art. 2 (new definitions, inserted by Art. 1(1))
key_provisions.summary: Defines 'environmental claim', 'generic environmental claim' (no specification given clearly and prominently on the same medium), 'sustainability label', 'certification scheme' and 'recognised excellent environmental performance'.

A claim about future environmental performance, including transition to carbon or climate neutrality, at product OR company level is misleading, case by case, unless backed by clear, objective, public, verifiable commitments in a detailed, realistic implementation plan. The plan must have measurable time-bound targets and allocated resources, and must be regularly verified by an independent third-party expert whose findings are available to consumers (Q&A Q6, Q12).

Displaying a sustainability label that is not based on a certification scheme or not established by public authorities is always banned. Q&A Q17: labels set up by non-EU public authorities count as banned unless they rest on a certification scheme.

Generic environmental claims are banned unless the trader can show recognised excellent environmental performance relevant to the claim. Q&A Q6: 'carbon-neutral', 'climate neutral', 'carbon compensated' and 'carbon positive' are treated as generic claims.
Banned: an environmental claim about the entire product or the trader's entire business when it concerns only one aspect of it.

Banned: claiming, based on GHG offsetting, that a PRODUCT has a neutral, reduced or positive GHG impact. Allowed only if the claim rests on the product's actual life-cycle impact within its own value chain. Q&A Q10: the ban does not cover company-level offset claims, but those stay subject to the general UCPD rules.
Banned: presenting requirements imposed by law on all products in the category as a distinctive feature of the trader's offer.

Corporate sustainability reports, including CSRD disclosures, are 'typically not in scope' because they are addressed to investors. The same content becomes in scope when reused in voluntary consumer-facing advertising or marketing.

Mandatory application for financial years starting on or after this date (secondary); early application for FY2026 permitted

items.status_note: The newest sources (mid-July to September 2026) describe the act as under Parliament and Council scrutiny: two months, extendable by two. Official Journal publication is not confirmed as of 13/10/2026.

key_provisions.summary: Large cut in mandatory datapoints (the team note cites EFRAG advice of a 61% reduction). Climate standard E1 keeps Scope 1/2/3 GHG disclosure.

claim_hooks: ESRS E1 climate disclosure / công bố khí hậu theo ESRS E1
Scope 3 emissions / phát thải phạm vi 3
items.evidence_note: DG FISMA CSRD page (fetched) lists '3 July 2026' adoption of two delegated acts: amendment of DR 2023/2772 and a voluntary standard for value-chain-cap undertakings; it also lists the 11/07/2025 quick fix. items.title: Commission Delegated Regulation establishing voluntary sustainability reporting standards for undertakings protected by the value-chain cap
items.title_vi: Chuẩn báo cáo bền vững tự nguyện, đồng thời là 'trần' thông tin doanh nghiệp EU được yêu cầu nhà cung cấp nhỏ (≤1.000 lao động) cung cấp
items.authority: European Commission

key_dates.what: Commission adopted the delegated act

items.status_note: Adopted 03/07/2026 together with the revised ESRS; OJ publication not confirmed in the sources found.

key_provisions.summary: Undertakings in the value chain with 1,000 or fewer employees may decline requests for sustainability information that go beyond these voluntary standards.

claim_hooks: VSME report / báo cáo bền vững theo chuẩn VSME
provided ESG data to EU customers / đã cung cấp dữ liệu ESG cho khách hàng EU
items.evidence_note: DG FISMA CSRD page (fetched): 3 July 2026 adoption of 'standards for voluntary use by undertakings protected by the value chain cap'. Cap wording from Linklaters.
items.relevance_why: Defines the practical ceiling of sustainability data that most Vietnamese exporting SMEs and mid-caps can be asked for by EU customers. It is a realistic reference set for SME-level Vietnamese sustainability disclosures.
items.caveats: Relationship to the earlier VSME recommendation (2025) not verified in this session.

items.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/73 amending the Taxonomy Disclosures, Climate and Environmental Delegated Acts (Taxonomy simplification)
items.title_vi: Đạo luật ủy quyền đơn giản hóa báo cáo theo Phân loại xanh EU (EU Taxonomy): ngưỡng trọng yếu 10%, giảm mạnh chỉ tiêu
items.authority: European Commission

key_dates.what: Adopted by the Commission
Published in the Official Journal (secondary)
Entry into force (secondary)
Applies; companies may keep the old rules for FY2025 reports if applied in full and disclosed (secondary)

do no significant harm (DNSH) / không gây hại đáng kể
items.evidence_note: DG FISMA taxonomy page (fetched): '4 July 2025: Adoption of a Delegated Act amending the Taxonomy Disclosures, Climate and Environmental Delegated Acts'; call for feedback 17/03/2026. Number 2026/73, OJ 08/01/2026, entry into force 28/01/2026, 10% threshold and datapoint reductions from Linklaters, BCLP and WPK.

sustainable fund / quỹ đầu tư bền vững
transition fund / quỹ chuyển đổi
Article 9 fund / quỹ Điều 9

items.caveats: Thresholds conflict between sources (15–20% taxonomy share vs 70% investment threshold); do not encode numbers until a final text exists.

items.title: Guidelines on funds' names using ESG or sustainability-related terms
items.title_vi: Hướng dẫn của ESMA về đặt tên quỹ có thuật ngữ ESG/bền vững (ngưỡng 80% và loại trừ PAB/CTB)

End of six-month transition for funds existing before 21/11/2024

items.relevance_why: A concrete, numeric benchmark for 'ESG fund' naming that Vietnamese fund managers do not face at home. Useful as a label convention for fund_esg_misrepresentation.
items.caveats: Applies to EU-domiciled UCITS/AIFs only.

Voluntary disclosure templates for other bonds marketed as environmentally sustainable and for sustainability-linked bonds.

green bond aligned with international standards / trái phiếu xanh theo chuẩn quốc tế

public_data.what: Check whether a reviewer named in a 'European Green Bond' claim is ESMA-registered (five firms at launch, per commentary).

items.evidence_note: ESMA news (fetched, dated 22/06/2026): register published, transitional regime under Arts 69–70 ended, reviewers now under ESMA supervision. Application date 21/12/2024 and OJ date from Matheson (secondary).

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2023/956 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023 establishing a carbon border adjustment mechanism
items.title_vi: Quy định Cơ chế điều chỉnh biên giới các-bon (CBAM): giai đoạn chính thức từ 01/01/2026
items.authority: European Parliament and Council of the European Union; European Commission (DG TAXUD)

key_dates.what: Transitional period (reporting only) began
Transitional period ended
Definitive regime applies
Sale of CBAM certificates via common central platform begins (secondary)
First annual CBAM declaration and certificate surrender for 2026 imports (secondary)

items.status_note: Definitive regime since 01/01/2026, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2083; downstream extension proposal in trilogue.

implemented_by: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2620 (free allocation adjustment and benchmarks)

key_provisions.summary: Imports of cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen.

Importers (authorised CBAM declarants) declare embedded emissions annually and surrender CBAM certificates priced on EU ETS auction prices. Actual emissions need verification by accredited verifiers; otherwise default values apply.

A carbon price effectively paid in the country of origin can be deducted. Vietnamese pilot allowances allocated free of charge (QĐ 263/QĐ-TTg) imply little or no deductible price (team inference, unverified).

claim_hooks: CBAM-ready / sẵn sàng đáp ứng CBAM
green steel / thép xanh
low-carbon steel / thép các-bon thấp
low-carbon cement / xi măng các-bon thấp
emission intensity x tCO2e per tonne of steel / cường độ phát thải x tCO2e/tấn thép
verified embedded emissions / phát thải hàm chứa đã được thẩm định
meets EU carbon border requirements / đáp ứng yêu cầu biên giới các-bon EU

public_data.name: DG TAXUD CBAM legislation and guidance page
public_data.what: Authoritative list of the CBAM legal acts (default values, verification, methodology); a source for checking claims that cite CBAM rules.

items.evidence_note: DG TAXUD pages (fetched): 'CBAM applies in its definitive regime from 1 January 2026'; transitional phase 2023–2025; price based on EU ETS auction prices; full list of implementing and delegated acts with numbers. Certificate sales and declaration dates from Mayer Brown, Crowe and a Commission tender notice (secondary).
items.relevance_why: Steel is a core Vietnamese export to the EU and a GreenScan test sector (HPG). CBAM makes 'green/low-carbon steel' and intensity claims checkable: compare the claimed tCO2e/t with Scope 1/2 and production in the same report and with EU default values.
items.caveats: Obligations fall on EU importers, not Vietnamese producers. Vietnamese producers supply verified installation data. 'CBAM-compliant' on a Vietnamese producer's own report is loose wording.

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 October 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/956 on the carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM simplification)
items.title_vi: Quy định đơn giản hóa CBAM: miễn trừ nhà nhập khẩu dưới 50 tấn/năm, giảm yêu cầu nắm giữ chứng chỉ xuống 50%
items.authority: European Parliament and Council of the European Union

key_dates.what: Parliament–Council political agreement (EP press release)
Council adoption (secondary)
Published in Official Journal (secondary)
Entry into force; Commission news on publication
Importers applying for authorised-declarant status by this date may keep importing provisionally pending decision (secondary)
CBAM certificate sales start (secondary)
First annual declaration and surrender, covering 2026 imports (secondary)

items.status_note: In force; changes apply to the definitive regime from 2026.

key_provisions.summary: Importers bringing in less than 50 tonnes per year of CBAM goods (by mass; not applicable to electricity and hydrogen, per EPRS) are exempt. This exempts about 90% of importers (EP) or about 182,000 importers (Commission) while keeping over 99% of embedded emissions covered.
Quarterly holding requirement lowered from 80% to 50% of embedded emissions imported since the start of the year, from 2027.
Annual declaration and certificate surrender by 30 September of the following year.
From 2027 the Commission may set default carbon prices for third countries with carbon pricing and publish the method.

claim_hooks: exempt from CBAM / được miễn CBAM
below CBAM threshold / dưới ngưỡng CBAM
CBAM cost / chi phí CBAM
carbon price paid in Vietnam deductible / giá các-bon đã trả tại Việt Nam được khấu trừ
items.evidence_note: DG TAXUD news (20/10/2025, fetched) gives the full title and date (8 October 2025), the 50 t exemption, about 182,000 importers exempt, over 99% emissions covered and default third-country carbon prices from 2027. EP press release (fetched) gives 'imports up to 50 tonnes per importer per year' and the 90% / 99% figures. Holding %, deadlines and OJ date from Mayer Brown, Crowe and PwC Malta.
items.relevance_why: The 50 t threshold applies per EU importer, not per Vietnamese exporter. A Vietnamese claim of being 'exempt from CBAM' because of small volumes needs checking against who imports and how much.
items.caveats: Article numbers not verified against the OJ text.

items.document_number: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 (corrected by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1740)
items.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 establishing the default values for the purposes of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 (CBAM default values)
items.title_vi: Quy định thực thi về giá trị phát thải mặc định CBAM theo quốc gia và sản phẩm
items.authority: European Commission

key_dates.what: Default values published (PwC Vietnam, secondary)

items.status_note: Listed by DG TAXUD as the act establishing default values, corrected by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1740. Used for the definitive period from 2026. The draft act foresaw a review of default values and mark-ups 'by December 2027 at the latest' (secondary).

key_provisions.summary: Country- and product-specific default embedded-emission intensities, based on the average intensity of each exporting country plus a mark-up.
10% in 2026, 20% in 2027, 30% from 2028 for steel, aluminium and cement; lower for fertilisers.

claim_hooks: emission intensity lower than EU default / cường độ phát thải thấp hơn giá trị mặc định của EU
tCO2e per tonne of product / tCO2e trên mỗi tấn sản phẩm

public_data.name: Annex of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621 (EUR-Lex)
public_data.what: Viet Nam-specific default embedded-emission values per CN code; a numeric benchmark to test claimed steel or cement intensity. Values were not extracted in this session.

items.evidence_note: DG TAXUD legislation page (fetched) lists IR 2025/2621 'establishes the default values' and IR 2026/1740 as its correction (primary for identity). Content (country-specific approach, mark-ups, publication date) from PwC Vietnam, Eurometal and a 2023 Commission transitional-period note (secondary).
items.relevance_why: This is the only official, product-level external benchmark for a Vietnamese steel or cement producer's claimed emission intensity. A large gap between a claimed intensity and the Viet Nam default value is a review signal.
items.caveats: Default values include a penalty mark-up and are not 'true' averages. Compare against the value before mark-up where possible; check the corrected annex (2026/1740).

items.title: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards the extension of its scope to downstream goods and anti-circumvention measures

items.title_vi: Quy định thực thi phân loại rủi ro quốc gia theo EUDR: Việt Nam thuộc nhóm 'rủi ro thấp'
items.authority: European Commission

key_dates.what: Country classification adopted and published
Classification starts to matter in practice when EUDR applies to large and medium operators

items.status_note: Viet Nam is listed as low risk on the Commission's EUDR country-classification page (checked 2026-10-13). A first review was reported for 2026; outcome not found. Destruction ban extends to medium-sized enterprises (secondary)

items.status_note: Framework in force. Product-specific ecodesign and Digital Product Passport requirements arrive through delegated acts under the 2025–2030 working plan (adopted April 2025). Per secondary sources, steel and iron acts are planned first (2026), then textiles, tyres and aluminium (2027).

key_provisions.summary: From 19/07/2026, large enterprises may not destroy unsold apparel, clothing accessories and footwear; 'destruction' includes recycling, other recovery and disposal. Defined derogations cover, for example, unsafe, damaged or irreparably defective goods.
Large enterprises disclose annually the quantity and reasons for discarding unsold consumer products in a standardised format.

Priority groups: steel and aluminium, textiles (apparel), furniture, tyres, mattresses, plus horizontal repairability and recyclability. Product information, including carbon and environmental footprint, mainly via the Digital Product Passport.

claim_hooks: digital product passport / hộ chiếu sản phẩm số
zero destruction of unsold goods / không tiêu hủy hàng tồn kho
circular fashion / thời trang tuần hoàn
product carbon footprint / dấu chân các-bon sản phẩm
recyclable garment / quần áo có thể tái chế
items.evidence_note: DG ENV ESPR page (fetched): 'In force since 18 July 2024'. EU Transition Pathways page (official EU site, fetched): DR 2026/296 and IR 2026/2 adopted 09/02/2026; ban from 19/07/2026 for large companies; medium-sized companies expected 2030; scope apparel, clothing accessories, footwear. IR 2026/2 OJ date and format application date from Cooley; working-plan priorities from secondary sources.
items.relevance_why: Vietnamese garment and footwear makers supply EU brands now bound by the destruction ban and disclosure. Future steel and textile delegated acts will set the product-footprint data Vietnamese exporters must provide, a hard source for later 'low-footprint product' claims.
items.caveats: Product-level requirements do not yet exist for most categories; avoid saying a product is 'ESPR-compliant' before its delegated act.

Aim: all packaging recyclable in an economically viable way by 2030 (article-level date not verified).

key_provisions.summary: Packaging must become recyclable in an economically viable way by 2030; recycled-content and reuse targets; restrictions on PFAS in food-contact packaging; harmonised EPR including a revised 'manufacturer' definition.

items.title: Bundesgerichtshof, Urteil vom 27. Juni 2024 – I ZR 98/23 (Werbung mit dem Begriff 'klimaneutral')
items.title_vi: Phán quyết Tòa án Liên bang Đức: quảng cáo 'trung hòa khí hậu' gây hiểu nhầm nếu không giải thích ngay trong quảng cáo là giảm thực hay bù trừ
items.authority: Bundesgerichtshof (I. Zivilsenat)

key_dates.what: Judgment; BGH press release Nr. 138/2024

items.status_note: Final judgment (appeal on points of law succeeded).

key_provisions.summary: 'klimaneutral' is ambiguous (reduction or offsetting). Given the high risk of misleading in environmental advertising, the ad itself must explain which is meant. Reduction takes priority over offsetting for climate protection, and an explanation only on a linked website is not enough.

claim_hooks: climate neutral production / sản xuất trung hòa khí hậu
all products climate neutral / tất cả sản phẩm trung hòa khí hậu
carbon neutral logo / logo trung hòa các-bon
items.evidence_note: BGH press release Nr. 138/2024 (fetched): case number, date, advertised sentence, reasoning quotes, outcome, lower-court dates. The defendant's name (Katjes) is from secondary sources; the press release anonymises it as '[die Beklagte]'.
items.relevance_why: Short, verbatim, offset-based neutrality claim with a clear holding. An ideal gold example for GreenScan's 'carbon neutral without stating reduction vs offset' pattern; the reasoning carries over to Vietnamese 'trung hòa các-bon' claims.
items.caveats: Pre-ECGT; after 27/09/2026 such product claims based on offsets are banned outright (UWG Annex 4c).

case.defendant: Katjes (German confectionery maker; anonymised in BGH press release, named in secondary sources)
case.claim_text_verbatim: Seit 2021 produziert [die Beklagte] alle Produkte klimaneutral
case.ruling_summary: Trade-journal ad and 'klimaneutral' logo found misleading under § 5(1) UWG because the ad did not explain whether neutrality came from emission reductions or offsetting (it came from supporting offset projects via a partner).
case.outcome: Appeal of the Wettbewerbszentrale upheld; Landgericht Kleve and OLG Düsseldorf rulings reversed; injunction against the advertising.
case.penalty: Injunction plus reimbursement of pre-litigation warning costs; no fine.

items.title: Tribunal judiciaire de Paris, 34e chambre, jugement du 23 octobre 2025, Greenpeace France, Les Amis de la Terre France et Notre Affaire à Tous c/ TotalEnergies SE et TotalEnergies Électricité et Gaz France
items.title_vi: Tòa án Paris xử TotalEnergies quảng cáo gây hiểu nhầm về 'tham vọng trung hòa các-bon vào 2050' và 'chủ thể lớn của chuyển dịch năng lượng'
items.authority: Tribunal judiciaire de Paris (34e chambre)

key_dates.what: First-instance judgment and court press release

items.status_note: First-instance judgment; appeal status as of 13/10/2026 not found.

key_provisions.ref: Code de la consommation art. L121-1 et seq. (UCPD transposition)
key_provisions.summary: Using 'carbon neutrality' terminology linked to the Paris Agreement, without telling consumers that the group followed its own scenario and kept increasing oil and gas production and investment, was misleading on the consumer website.

claim_hooks: ambition to reach carbon neutrality by 2050 / tham vọng đạt trung hòa các-bon vào năm 2050
net zero 2050 / phát thải ròng bằng 0 vào 2050
major player in the energy transition / doanh nghiệp tiên phong trong chuyển dịch năng lượng
aligned with the Paris Agreement / phù hợp Thỏa thuận Paris
items.evidence_note: Court communiqué PDF (dated 23/10/2025, text extracted locally): RG number, the quoted claims, legal basis, reasoning, orders (cease, damages, publication of the operative part), rejected claims on fossil gas and agrofuels. Monetary amounts (EUR 8,000 per NGO, EUR 15,000 costs, a per-day penalty reported as EUR 10,000 or 20,000) are secondary and conflicting.
items.relevance_why: The closest analogue to Vietnamese energy and power companies' 'Net Zero 2050' and 'tiên phong chuyển dịch năng lượng' statements. It shows that a net-zero ambition alongside expanding fossil output can be misleading when the gap is not disclosed. Strong gold example for future_target and omission.
items.caveats: Only consumer-website communications were caught; 'institutional' communications on gas and agrofuels were outside this action. That distinction matters for annual reports.

case.defendant: TotalEnergies SE and TotalEnergies Électricité et Gaz France
case.claim_text_verbatim: leur ambition d'atteindre la neutralité carbone d'ici 2050 et d'être un acteur majeur dans la transition énergétique
case.ruling_summary: Claims of a 2050 carbon-neutrality ambition and of being a major energy-transition player, made on totalenergies.fr after the rebranding, misled consumers. The Paris-Agreement terminology implied alignment with scientific recommendations to cut fossil production immediately, while the group kept increasing oil and gas output and investment and did not disclose its own scenario.
case.outcome: Partly upheld: cease the misleading communication, damages to the NGOs for moral harm, publication of the operative part on the commercial website. Claims on fossil gas and agrofuels and the ecological-damage claim were rejected.
case.penalty: Damages and costs; per-day penalty for non-compliance (amounts per secondary sources, conflicting).

AGCM press release

key_provisions.summary: Vague, generic or overly emphatic environmental claims, and misleading or omissive ones, about circularity, recyclability, 'green' fibres and decarbonisation targets, are unfair practices.

claim_hooks: circular system design / thiết kế hệ thống tuần hoàn
recyclable products / sản phẩm có thể tái chế
made from sustainable materials / làm từ vật liệu bền vững
cut GHG emissions 25% by 2030 / giảm 25% phát thải khí nhà kính vào 2030
net zero by 2050 / phát thải ròng bằng 0 vào 2050

case.defendant: Infinite Styles Services Co. Ltd (operator of SHEIN's European websites)
case.ruling_summary: Environmental claims on SHEIN's EU sites were vague, generic or overly emphatic, or misleading and omissive. evoluSHEIN 'green fibres' claims implied the line used only sustainable, fully recyclable materials and hid that it is a marginal share of the offer. GHG targets (-25% by 2030, zero by 2050) were vague and contradicted by rising emissions in 2023 and 2024.
case.outcome: Practice found unfair; fine imposed; company says it revised its website and review processes.
